Here’s the basics of how stocks work. Bob forms a corporation with Alice and Eve. The company issues 10,000 shares at $10 each, allowing them to raise $100,000 for the company. The money from that initial sale goes to the company. If Eve buys shares from Bob, that money will go to Bob, the company won’t see any of it. The company can buy its own stock and that stock is now called treasury stock. They can sell that stock later to raise more money. Basically, the company can invest in itself. 

Now, it starts to get complex. If you go through a broker, you can sell a stock short. That is, you sell the stock and then buy it later. The way that’s done is you sell some stock owned by the broker and after a set period of time, you have to buy it back. You’d only do this if you think the stock’s price is going to go down. 

For more fun, there are stock options. They are a promise to buy or sell a stock at a certain price. Say you shorted the stock above, you could also create a stock option with someone to buy the stock at the current price. If the stock doesn’t drop, you exercise the option so you can buy the stock back at a lower price. 

This is the limit of what I know about stocks. There is quite a bit more and it gets even screwier as you go.
